title: Caller on Line Two
excerpt: At 2:14 a.m., the switchboard lights up, and tomorrow calls in.
content:
The call came in at 2:14 a.m., which was normal. What the caller said was not.

"Tomorrow morning," the voice said, calm as a weather report, "the 7:42 freight will stop at the old tannery spur. It doesn't stop there. It hasn't in eleven years. You'll want to be on the overpass at 7:40, not earlier — the first two cars are carrying more than cargo."

"Who is this?" Ada asked, hand already moving to the dump switch.

"You've had this frequency for three weeks," the voice said. "Tonight is the first night you'll believe me. That's not a threat. It's arithmetic."

The line went to dead air the way lines do — suddenly, and then completely.

At 7:42 the next morning, the 7:42 freight stopped at the old tannery spur. It stayed for six minutes. When it pulled out, two of its cars were empty, and the overpass had one more person on it than the schedule accounted for: Ada, holding her phone, recording, exactly as instructed, exactly at 7:40.

Her producer wanted the tape. The police wanted the tape. The station's lawyers wanted the tape so badly they could taste it.

But when she played it back that night, alone in the booth with the fader levels breathing like a sleeping animal, the call wasn't on the recording.

There was only her voice, filling the silence the way hosts do:

"...and up next, at 2:14, we go to the phones. Line two, you're on The Quiet Frequency."
